sections.content:
You know relative superlatives (*el/la más* + adjective) and regular *-ísimo* (*utilísimo*) from B1 Unit 7. Art criticism refines both patterns for nuance and register:

• Relative superlative + *que* + subjunctive: when a superlative evaluates the highest degree within a reviewer's experience, the relative clause usually takes the present perfect or present subjunctive (*Es la retrospectiva más ambiciosa que haya acogido este museo*, *Es el trazo más preciso que conozca el público local*).
• Spelling changes in *-ísimo*: adjectives in *-co/-ca* change to *-quísimo* (*rico* → *riquísimo*), and adjectives in *-io* simplify *-i-* (*amplio* → *amplísimo*).
• **Measured intensity**: formal reviews often prefer *sumamente* + adjective (*sumamente sobria*, *sumamente desigual*) over *-ísimo*, which can sound overly enthusiastic.

sections.title: Refined superlatives in critical prose
rows: la muestra más coherente que haya visto
the most coherent exhibition I have seen (que + subjunctive)
an extremely rich palette of nuances (c -> qu)
un recorrido amplísimo por su trayectoria
a very broad survey of her career (-io -> -ísimo)
an exceedingly uneven final room (measured register)

items.spanish: Es la retrospectiva más completa que haya organizado el museo municipal.
items.english: It is the most complete retrospective that the municipal museum has organised.

items.spanish: La artista domina una paleta cromática riquísima sin caer en el exceso.
items.english: The artist masters an extraordinarily rich colour palette without falling into excess.

items.spanish: El trazo revela una maestría sumamente sobria en las piezas de formato pequeño.
items.english: The stroke reveals an exceedingly restrained mastery in the small-format pieces.

items.spanish: La textura del papel ofrece un contraste amplísimo entre zonas claras y oscuras.
items.english: The texture of the paper offers a very wide contrast between light and dark areas.

sections.content: English uses a normal indicative verb after 'the best ... that I have ever seen', so learners often write indicative *que ha acogido* in formal Spanish reviews. In C1 criticism, pair the relative superlative with the subjunctive (*que haya acogido*) when making a sweeping evaluative judgement, and watch the spelling change in *riquísimo* (never *ricísimo*).
